| 2026-05-17 | **Event guest-count change flow — monotonic ratchet with vendor confirmation on increases, decreases blocked outright.** Guest count is a numeric attribute, not a swap, so the state machine diverges from § 10 / § 11 in two material ways: **(1)** changes are **direction-restricted** — couples can increase the planning guest count but cannot decrease it once any guest-count-dependent vendor has confirmed at that count. The minus stepper on the guest-count field is disabled at the UI layer with hint *"Cannot decrease below confirmed floor — vendors have already committed to N guests"* (mirrors the disabled-CTA pattern from § 2.2d.i self-review block). **(2)** the change touches only **guest-count-dependent vendors** — a per-vendor flag (`is_guest_count_dependent`) captured at onboarding (0006) marks which vendors plan against the count: defaults TRUE for catering, florals, mobile bar, lights & sound, name cards, favors, printable invites; defaults FALSE for photography, videography, HMUA, planner, broadcast. Only dependent vendors receive the confirmation card and only their capacity / pricing recalculates. **Ratchet enforcement:** floor = MAX(all confirmed counts ever in this event's history). New vendors booked later inherit the current floor as their starting commitment. Vendor back-out dissolves THAT vendor's commitment but the floor for remaining dependent vendors stays — couples cannot reduce because other vendors are still planning at the higher count. **Confirmation gate (only on increase):** modal surfaces per-vendor cost impact (e.g., "+20 plates × ₱1,200 = +₱24,000 for Casa Manila Catering") and total delta before vendor cards fire. **Per-vendor check is a capacity check** — does this vendor have the headcount capacity at the current proximity to event? Customer-facing messaging: *"Your guest count change is available for all vendors. Waiting for their confirmation."* OR *"Your guest count change is available for X vendors but exceeds capacity for Y vendors. We cannot apply this change until all vendors accept."* Same chat negotiation / mediation tier / 48 hr · 72 hr timeouts / race condition handling as § 10. **Decrease override:** couples experiencing genuine catastrophic cancellation (force majeure, mass family withdrawal) can request a floor reduction via 0029 help center → admin mediator works with each affected vendor case-by-case to negotiate downward; default behavior remains decrease-blocked. Locked into iteration 0021 § 12 (new section). | Caterers, florists, printers, and mobile-bar operators commit inventory + crew based on the guest count: ingredients pre-ordered, centerpieces fabricated, name cards printed, crew rostered. A late decrease causes irrecoverable financial loss for the vendor (perishable inventory + non-refundable supplier deposits) without a corresponding refund for the couple. The ratchet protects vendor margin while preserving couple flexibility on the only direction that's still possible (upward — vendors can scale up by sourcing more inventory). Direction-restriction is enforced at the UI rather than negotiated through the state machine because it's not a "vendor preference" issue — it's a physical commitment-of-inventory issue that mediation cannot reverse. The admin-override path covers genuine catastrophes where the couple has no alternative. Affects iterations: 0021 (canonical spec, new § 12), 0006 (vendor side — `is_guest_count_dependent` flag + per-head rate · capacity ceiling at proximity-to-event · capacity confirmation card), 0019 (chat infrastructure — same structured-card dependency as § 10), 0023 (admin mediation tier — decrease-override workflow), 0034 (per-head delta charges → existing milestone-payment flow). |
| 2026-05-17 | **Per-vendor change-acceptance cutoffs — vendors set three cutoff windows (date / venue / guest count) at onboarding; if any confirmed vendor is past their cutoff for the change type, the standard change flow is blocked outright and routes to admin override.** Each vendor record carries three fields captured at onboarding (0006): `date_change_cutoff_days_before_event`, `venue_change_cutoff_days_before_event`, `guest_count_change_cutoff_days_before_event` (NULL when vendor isn't dependent on the attribute). **V1 ships with conservative category-based defaults pre-filled at vendor account creation** — vendors edit in 0022 Settings: catering 30/21/14 days · florals 21/14/10 · mobile bar 21/14/7 · lights & sound 14/21/7 · photography 7/3/NULL · videography 7/3/NULL · HMUA 7/3/NULL · planner 7/3/7 · live stream / broadcast 3/3/NULL · name cards/favors/print 21/14/10. **Pre-flight gate on every change attempt** (date / venue / guest count): before the § 10.1 / § 11.1 / § 12.3 confirmation modal fires, the system checks each confirmed vendor's cutoff for the change type vs current proximity to event date. If any vendor is past their cutoff, the standard flow is blocked with a dedicated modal listing the blocking vendors + their cutoff dates + a "Request admin override" CTA — no reason field, no vendor cards. Admin override is the only forward path. **In-flight protection:** changes initiated BEFORE the cutoff date and currently pending continue to run to completion even if the cutoff falls during the negotiation window; cutoffs apply to NEW attempts, not in-progress ones (otherwise mid-window cutoff transitions would auto-fail valid changes). **Retroactivity rule:** vendor edits to their cutoffs in 0022 do NOT apply retroactively to already-confirmed bookings. Cutoffs in effect at booking-confirmation time are snapshotted to `vendor_event_window.effective_date_cutoff` / `effective_venue_cutoff` / `effective_guest_count_cutoff` and become binding for that event. Prevents vendors from quietly shortening their acceptance window mid-engagement to block the couple. **Admin override (only forward path past cutoff):** couple files via 0029 help center → admin mediator reaches out to each past-cutoff vendor individually → if vendors agree, mediator applies the change via 0023 admin console; if vendors decline, the couple's only remaining option is to cancel that vendor's booking and find a replacement. Override actions log to `dispute_resolutions` with `cause = 'past_cutoff_override'`. **Out of scope:** cutoffs apply only to vendor bookings — Setnayan platform SKUs (Papic, Panood, Patiktok, LED, AI Highlights, etc.) have their own pre-event activation / rendering / fulfillment windows handled separately by the per-SKU flows. Locked into iteration 0021 § 13 (new section) with cross-references added to § 10, § 11, § 12. | Vendor margin protection: as the event approaches, vendors progressively commit inventory and crew — catering buys ingredients, florists buy flowers, lights & sound rosters crew, printers run name cards. Late-stage changes can be unrecoverable financial losses. The cutoff lets vendors declare upfront what proximity is too late for what kind of change, removing the negotiation tax (and the awkward "we have to say no" interaction) for changes that are physically impossible to accommodate at that proximity. **Defaults eliminate vendor configuration burden** for the common case — most catering vendors won't think to set a cutoff manually, but the V1 seed values match industry norms (caterers commonly lock headcount 14 days out; photographers can adapt to date changes within a week). **The retroactivity rule closes an adversarial edge case** — without it, a vendor unhappy with a potential reschedule could shorten their cutoff to 90 days the moment they sensed friction, instantly blocking the couple. Snapshotting cutoffs at booking confirmation means the terms that existed when the couple chose this vendor are the binding ones. **Admin override preserves couple agency** for genuine emergencies (typhoon, venue collapse, family crisis) while keeping the default flow tight and protecting vendors from frivolous late-stage requests. Affects iterations: 0021 (canonical spec, new § 13 + cross-refs in § 10/§ 11/§ 12), 0006 (vendor onboarding — three new cutoff fields with category-based defaults), 0022 (vendor dashboard — Change Acceptance Policy settings panel · NOT retroactive to confirmed bookings), 0023 (admin override workflow + `dispute_resolutions.cause = 'past_cutoff_override'`), 0029 (help center — past-cutoff override request form). |

Shared helper module `apps/web/lib/contracts.ts` (types, validators, formatters). **Signing-order policy:** either party can sign first once the contract is sent; the trigger seals when both rows exist. **SKU retirement:** `contract_intelligence_upgrade` (couple ₱199) + `contract_intelligence_per_contract` (vendor ₱199) flipped to is_active=FALSE in service_catalog; both added to `RETIRED_SKU_CODES` in `apps/web/lib/sku-catalog.ts`. `vendor_pro_weekly` description updated to remove the stale "free Contract Intelligence" perk and reference the new built-in e-signature flow instead. **Anthropic Console scope shrinks** but the workspace stays (Concierge brain paid tier still needs Haiku 4.5 per 2026-05-18 row 1). **V1.1 follow-ups noted inline (TODO comments):** PDF stamping (compositing signature images directly onto the PDF page rather than displaying them side-by-side), email notifications when a vendor sends a contract for signature, audit-trail export. | Owner directive 2026-05-18 — "remove the contract part completely. but still let the vendor upload a contract file in pdf. and we have the option to let them sign and the customer sign, and also offer legal notary for this. we will have an inhouse notary that can cater this? or that is not allowed since vendor may be from a different city?" Two reasons drove the simplification. **First, the AI-analysis SKU was paid scope (₱199/contract) that adds compliance + LLM-cost risk for marginal value** — every couple needs to upload-and-sign a vendor contract regardless of whether they want AI analysis, so making the underlying sign flow free + first-class is the more durable V1 surface. List pages on both sides + the publish CTA label ("Make visible to couple") reinforce the same framing. **(4) Why the owner made this call** (drivers behind the further shrink, beyond the verbatim quote above). **First, signing isn't Setnayan's core competency** — wedding-planning artifacts (timeline, vendor pack, Concierge wizard, Save-the-Date, Panood, Patiktok) are the value Setnayan ships; e-signature is a commodity feature already solved by DocuSign · HelloSign · Adobe Sign · Signaturit · plus free workarounds (emailing a signed scan, in-person signing at vendor meetings) that the wedding industry already uses comfortably. Building it in-house gates Setnayan against best-in-class e-sig tooling for no upside, and bundling it as a Setnayan feature signals to couples + vendors that the app is the contract authority — which it isn't. **Second, liability scope shrinks substantially.** A dual-sig flow where Setnayan captures + stores signature PNGs + IP + UA + signed_at + serves them via signed URLs makes Setnayan an arguable party to the contract's execution (or at minimum a custodian of e-signature evidence) under Philippine Electronic Commerce Act (RA 8792) + Rules on Electronic Evidence — even with disclaimers, a couple or vendor in dispute could subpoena Setnayan as evidence custodian, force preservation orders, and surface the platform as a third-party in litigation. Pure document hosting (PDF storage with view/download access) keeps Setnayan in the same posture as Dropbox or Google Drive — a passive document host with no signature authority. **Third, simpler UX for both sides.** Vendors already upload signed PDFs to clients via email constantly — adding a "sign in Setnayan" step is friction, not value. Couples likewise prefer to read + sign on their own time + with their own tooling (e.g., printing for traditional ink signature with family witnesses present, as is common in Filipino wedding contracts). The Setnayan flow shrinks to upload → publish → both sides can see/download → done, which fits naturally alongside the chat thread where the contract was negotiated. **Fourth, couples and vendors handle signing flows wherever they prefer** — the spec does not need to pick a signing UX for the entire ecosystem; the wedding industry's existing patterns (email signed PDFs, in-person at venue site visits, separate e-sig tool for traveling couples) cover the spectrum without Setnayan opining. | 2026-05-22 | **Fix: Reception planning-group Search showed Ceremony churches above target section (Task #47 · PR [#310](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/310) merged 2026-05-22).** Fourth 2026-05-22 row · live-bug report from owner during V1 marketplace testing: *"i am searching for reception venue and the churches still showed. they are not qualified because they are design for ceremonies"*. **Root cause** (none of the 4 initial candidates exactly — actual cause was page-level rendering scope): `/vendors` rendered the full 12-folder catalog on every visit regardless of how the user arrived. `WEDDING_FOLDER_ORDER` lists Ceremony first (with `<PairedVenuePanel>` page-level + `<CeremonyVenuesSection>` inside the Ceremony folder showing church/mosque/INC-chapel/civil-registrar cards from `venue_directory`), then Reception. When dashboard event-home Reception planning-group [Search] button routed to `/vendors#reception`, the browser scroll-anchored to the Reception `<section id="reception">` heading — but the entire Ceremony folder + the page-level PairedVenuePanel sat directly above. One scroll-up of the mouse wheel revealed Manila Cathedral, INC chapels, etc. — the user reasonably perceived churches as appearing in Reception. The folder-render conditional (`isCeremony = folder === 'ceremony'`) inside `CatalogView` was already structurally correct; the bug was missing page-level scoping. **Fix:** added `?folder=<slug>` query param parsed in `parseFilters` against the canonical 12-folder enum (`WEDDING_FOLDER_ORDER`). When present and valid, `CatalogView` (a) suppresses `<PairedVenuePanel>` unless scope is ceremony/null, (b) filters the folder-render loop to ONLY emit the scoped folder section, (c) renders a new `<ScopedFolderBanner>` with polite brand voice (no dev text per [[feedback_setnayan_no_dev_text_post_launch]]) and a "Browse all folders" escape link. `FolderTabs` stay visible so user can pivot without back-navigating. Dashboard `planning-groups.tsx` `searchHref` updated from `/vendors#<slug>` → `/vendors?folder=<slug>#<slug>` so the param scopes the render AND the anchor preserves smooth-scroll-into-section. Universal Browse entries (top-nav, sitemap, direct visit) unchanged — full 12-folder catalog renders. **Architectural preservation:** CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row 470 (12-folder marketplace remap with Reception as filter-only via `venue_setting`, Ceremony with `venue_directory` curated venues) and 2026-05-19 row 425 (per-category schemas / 192 sub-categories) untouched. No schema change, no data-model change — Ceremony venues are still in `venue_directory`, Reception venues are still `vendor_profiles` filtered by `venue_setting`. The fix is purely render-scope at the page level. **Audit per owner directive** ("audit other 11 folders for same class of bug"): `venue_directory` data flows ONLY through `PairedVenuePanel` (page-level, now gated) + `CeremonyVenuesSection` (inside Ceremony folder only, already correct). No other folder leaks church/mosque/civil-registrar content. The other 10 non-venue folders (planning_logistics_travel · photo_video · catering · attire · hair_makeup · music_program · decor_florals_sound · rings_accessories · booths_stations · invitations_keepsakes) also benefit from scope when reached via dashboard Search — clean single-folder focus instead of universal-catalog-with-target-folder-buried-among-11-others. **Entry points (orphan-prevention rule [[feedback_setnayan_orphan_prevention]]):** (a) `/vendors` top-nav Browse / sitemap / direct visit → unscoped full catalog unchanged; (b) `/vendors?folder=<slug>#<slug>` from 12 planning-group [Search] buttons on `/dashboard/[eventId]` → new scoped view; (c) `/vendors?folder=invalid` typo → falls back to unscoped catalog (parseFilters validates against `WEDDING_FOLDER_ORDER`); (d) `FolderTabs` chips in scoped mode → hash-only nav, "Browse all folders" link clears scope. **Cross-references:** CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row 470 (12-folder marketplace remap) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row "Home is the guide" (Search button intent is to land on a specific group's vendors, not universal catalog) · Task #46 row (PR [#309](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/309) "Fix: Add to plan failing on venue_directory cards" — shipped same day, complementary venue_directory surface). **No new orphans introduced or caught** — all changes are render-scope refinements on existing routes. **Affected files:** `apps/web/app/vendors/page.tsx` (Props.searchParams.folder?: string · parseFilters returns folder: WeddingFolder | null · CatalogView gains scopedFolder prop · PairedVenuePanel gating · folder-loop filtering · new ScopedFolderBanner component, ~77 net lines added); Without this flag, those picks would silently stay in the plan, leak into the Compare view + the day-of timeline, and ambush the host at lock-in. **Three issue kinds, ranked by severity:** (1) `religion` — marketplace-linked vendor's `vendor_profiles.compatible_ceremony_types[]` doesn't include host's current `ceremony_type` → chip reads *"Your wedding is now Civil — this vendor doesn't match."* (2) `venue_setting` — marketplace-linked vendor's `vendor_profiles.compatible_venue_settings[]` doesn't include host's current `venue_setting` → chip reads *"Your reception is now a garden — this vendor doesn't cover that setting."* (3) `directory` — picks linked via `event_vendors.source_venue_directory_id` (not `marketplace_vendor_id`) where `venue_directory.compatible_ceremony_types[]` mismatches → chip reads *"Your wedding is now Civil — this venue doesn't host that ceremony."* **Precedence: religion > venue_setting > directory.** A marketplace vendor failing both religion AND venue_setting surfaces the religion mismatch (more semantically severe). Venue-only mismatches surface only when religion would pass. **Null array convention** (open-to-all safety valve): an empty `compatible_*` array OR NULL column treats the vendor as compatible — same OR-clause shape as PR #305's `/vendors` religion-default-on filter (`compat IS NULL OR compat @> ARRAY[host_value]`). Protects legacy / pre-iteration-0043 vendor rows from false-positive flags. **Off-platform / custom rows** (no `marketplace_vendor_id` AND no `source_venue_directory_id`) → no compat data exists → chip never renders. **Data fetch strategy:** extended the `event_vendors` SELECT in `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/page.tsx` to include `marketplace_vendor_id` + `source_venue_directory_id` (no schema change — columns already exist via migrations `20260519200000_vendor_invites_foundation.sql` + `20260530000000_event_vendors_venue_directory_link.sql`). Two follow-up batch queries against `vendor_profiles` + `venue_directory` resolve the compat arrays via `.in('vendor_profile_id', marketplaceIds)` + `.in('venue_directory_id', directoryIds)`. At most 2 extra round trips per page render even for events with 50+ picks — mirrors the fetch pattern in `apps/web/lib/venue-recommendations.ts` (PR #309 lineage). Both helper queries use the existing `adminClient` since `vendor_profiles` + `venue_directory` are public-read tables. **Brand voice — amber not red.** This is informational, not an error. The vendor was a valid pick when the host saved them; the *event* changed underneath them, so the chip reads as a heads-up not a scolding. AlertTriangle icon + amber-50/60 background + amber-300/50 border + Remove button styled as a calm cream-filled border-amber-400/60 micro-button. Per [[feedback_setnayan_no_dev_text_post_launch]] — no jargon, no inline parens, just one polite sentence + a single-word action. **Remove flow:** reuses the existing `deleteVendor` server action in `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors/actions.ts` (host clicks Remove → form submits hidden `event_id` + `vendor_id` → server action runs under host's RLS session → row hard-deleted from `event_vendors` → revalidates both `/dashboard/[eventId]` AND `/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors` so chip vanishes without a hard refresh). The `CompatibilityChip` is a sub-element of an existing card pick row; it renders only when `pick.compatibility_issue` is non-null. Remove form wires to the existing `deleteVendor` server action — no new routes, no new endpoints, no new orphan risk. **Test plan:** `pnpm -F web typecheck` clean · `pnpm -F web lint` no new warnings (same pre-existing in `color-range-manipulator.tsx`) · visual smoke pending post-deploy preview but covers: (a) Catholic event with Catholic church pick → no chip (compatible); (b) flip ceremony_type → Civil via CeremonyTypeChip modal → Catholic church pick now shows amber chip + Remove button; (c) Garden `venue_setting` event with indoor-only-tagged band → chip with venue mismatch + Remove; (d) click Remove → row + chip vanish, no full page refresh, counter math adjusts; (e) off-platform vendor with both FKs null → no chip regardless of event drift. **Affected files** (4 files net +429/-51): `apps/web/lib/wedding-plan-groups.ts` (PlanCardCompatibilityIssue type + EventVendorRowInput shape + computeCompatibilityIssue algorithm + readable-label tables + bucketVendorsByGroup widened signature) · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/page.tsx` (extend events SELECT to include `venue_setting` · extend event_vendors SELECT to include `marketplace_vendor_id` + `source_venue_directory_id` · two batch-fetch queries for compat data · enrich event_vendors rows before PlanningGroups consumes them · pass `venueSetting` + `ceremonyType` props) · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/_components/planning-groups.tsx` (thread `venueSetting` prop · pass to bucketVendorsByGroup · new CompatibilityChip sub-component with AlertTriangle icon + amber palette + form action=deleteVendor) · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors/actions.ts` (deleteVendor now also revalidates `/dashboard/[eventId]` event-home path so chip vanishes without hard refresh). **Auto-merge** per [[feedback_setnayan_pr_auto_merge]] — `gh pr merge 315 --auto --merge` armed immediately after creation. **Cross-references:** CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 9 above (PR #314 PR A — Dimensions 1+2+4 ship same session) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 5 (PR #305 religion-default-on filter on /vendors — same compatibility shape; Owner directive verbatim: *"desktop mode will have 2 columns (to maximize screen size) while mobile mode will only have 1 column."* **(1) Change.** Grid class on the tier-loop `<ul>` rewrote from `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4` → `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2`. Mobile (<640px) keeps grid-cols-1 unchanged; sm: (≥640px) + every wider breakpoint locks at grid-cols-2; the lg: (1024px) jump to 3 cols + xl: (1280px) jump to 4 cols are removed. **(2) Why.** With 12 planning cards grouped across 4 tiers (per [[CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 "Home is the guide" row]] · latest-by floors + front-load compression + completed-tasks-sink), each card carries a title + religion-adaptive hint copy (from PR #314 · 2026-05-22 row 9) + status pill + tone-coded badge + pick list with possible incompatibility chip (from PR #315 · 2026-05-22 row 10). At lg/xl breakpoints each card was 240-340px wide which forced the religion-adaptive Muslim hint copy + Catholic pre-Cana paperwork hint + similar long-copy lines to wrap awkwardly into 3+ lines. At sm: 2-col the cards are 320-630px wide depending on viewport — enough horizontal room for the longest religion-adaptive copy + the pick list previews + the inline incompatibility chip. Trade-off accepted: laptops + wide monitors now show 2-col stack instead of 4-col grid, which means the page is taller on a 1440px viewport — but per the owner directive *"maximize screen size"* refers to per-card horizontal real-estate, not vertical density. Vertical scroll is OK; cramped cards are not. **(3) Entry points (orphan-prevention per [[feedback_setnayan_orphan_prevention]]):** `/dashboard/[eventId]` event home — every host's first surface after login per [[project_setnayan_login_landing]]. Fix: hoist `flatPalette` out of the IIFE to the data-prep block + render both components as flat top-level JSX siblings. The IIFE was the fragile pattern; flat top-level JSX is the reliable shape. Architecture insight captured for future sessions. **(2) PR #451 figure polish (closed/superseded by #453).** Rebuilt Silhouette function with 6-layer rendering: (1) ground shadow ellipse beneath feet · (2) hair path BEHIND head (long flowing for dress; short cropped for suit/barong) · (3) skin-tone head circle (r=6 vs prior r=5 for better proportions) · (4) body path with smooth bezier curves per attire type (fitted bodice + A-line skirt on dress, jacket + trousers + hinted leg split on suit, loose vertical with subtle bell hem on barong) · (5) per-attire detail overlays (neckline V on dress, lapel V + tie on suit, embroidery dashed line on barong) · (6) two small shoe ovals at the foot. Canvas got radial gradient + decorative pointed-arch SVG at bottom. ViewBox 0 0 28 92 for elegant tall proportions (vs prior 24 60 which produced squat cartoonish figures). PR #451 was closed in favor of PR #453 which subsumed all of #451's polish PLUS the new style-themes work. **(3) PR #453 StyleTheme system.** Style picker chips were inert toggles; this PR wires each chip to a concrete `StyleTheme` record that drives visible aesthetic changes. Path 2 ships smart defaults today without schema work; Path 1 (event-level toggles + role defaults · `events.schedule_includes_cocktails / _after_party / _rehearsal_dinner` booleans) deferred until owner picks the event-level scope. **Why the change matters:** prior behavior hardcoded `defaultChecked={block === 'ceremony' || block === 'reception'}` for every guest regardless of role — every VIP forced 3+ extra clicks (cocktails + after-party + rehearsal dinner). At typical Filipino wedding sizes (50-300 guests · ~10-20 inner-circle) that's 30-60 wasted clicks per event for the inner circle alone, plus another 1 click per non-inner-circle guest (cocktails). Per the Filipino-wedding-reality analysis: 95-100% of guests attend ceremony + reception + cocktails regardless of role; only the inner circle attends after-party + rehearsal-dinner by default. **Schema (zero changes):** no new columns · no new tables · no new SKU · `invited_${block}` checkbox names on the form stay identical so server actions consume them unchanged. **Code (4 files net +182/-37):** `apps/web/lib/guests.ts` — new `INNER_CIRCLE_ROLES` `ReadonlySet<GuestRole>` (12 roles: bride · groom · bride_parents · groom_parents · bride_immediate_family · groom_immediate_family · maid_of_honor · matron_of_honor · best_man · bridesmaid · groomsman · principal_sponsor) + new exported `defaultInvitedToForRole(role: GuestRole): InvitedToBlock[]` helper (returns 5-block array for inner-circle roles, 3-block array `['ceremony', 'reception', 'cocktails']` for everyone else). `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/_components/invited-to-chips.tsx` — NEW client island. Listens to the role `<select id="role">` on the same page via `document.getElementById` + `addEventListener('change')`. On mount: populates from `initialBlocks` (edit form · existing guest's saved value) OR `defaultInvitedToForRole(initialRole)` (new form · no saved value yet). On role change after mount: snaps chips to the new role's defaults. Controlled checkboxes (React `checked` prop) so Tailwind `has-[:checked]:` selectors still flip the chip background on snap. `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/new/page.tsx` — swaps hardcoded chip JSX for `<InvitedToChips roleSelectId="role" initialRole="guest"/>`. Drops now-unused `INVITED_TO_BLOCKS` + `INVITED_TO_LABELS` imports. Hint copy updated from *"Default: ceremony + reception. Toggle off any block the guest isn't invited to"* to *"Picks smart defaults from the Role above. Toggle any block the guest isn't invited to."* `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/[guestId]/page.tsx` — same swap with `<InvitedToChips roleSelectId="role" initialRole={guest.role} initialBlocks={initialInvited}/>` where `initialInvited` filters `guest.invited_to_blocks` (schema column is `string[]`) to valid `InvitedToBlock` values via type guard. Removes `INVITED_TO_LABELS` import (kept `INVITED_TO_BLOCKS` for the filter). **Snap-on-role-change behavior:** when host changes Role dropdown AFTER mount, chips snap to the new role's defaults. Host's prior manual toggles on the OLD role get reset — intentional trade-off because role change implies "this person's attendance scope is different now" (e.g., changing a guest from `bridesmaid` to `coin_sponsor` should reset after-party + rehearsal-dinner off, not keep them on by accident). Host can re-toggle individual chips after the snap. **Snap-NOT-on-mount behavior for edit form:** when `initialBlocks` is provided (edit form with existing guest data), chips populate from the saved value on first render — no snap. The snap only fires on subsequent role changes via the change-event listener. This preserves existing data correctly while still delivering smart defaults on role changes. **Inner-circle rationale:** the 12 roles chosen are the ones who attend after-party + rehearsal dinner in Filipino wedding reality (couple themselves · parents who host the event · immediate family who fly in · primary wedding party who's there for the prep + after · principal sponsors who're peer-witnesses). Secondary sponsors (candle/veil/cord/coin) typically attend ceremony only — they're peer-honors not full-event family; bearers + flower girl are kids whose parents manage their attendance separately; officiant + readers + soloist have ceremony roles but typically aren't invited to post-event social blocks. Host can still toggle on/off per individual guest where needed. **Cross-references:** CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row § "VIP family roles" PR #424 (added the 4 VIP family roles that are part of the inner-circle set) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row § "Concierge dual-scope trial" (similar client-island pattern · `document.getElementById` + `useEffect` listener on form interactions) · existing `INVITED_TO_BLOCKS` constant in `lib/guests.ts` (5-block enum order: ceremony · reception · cocktails · after_party · rehearsal_dinner — unchanged). **Path 1 still pending owner decision** (event-level toggles via `events.schedule_includes_cocktails / _after_party / _rehearsal_dinner` booleans). If/when owner picks Path 1, this PR's smart defaults stay correct — they only fire when the underlying event has the block enabled, which is the default behavior anyway. The schema additions can land independently without breaking this work. **Affected files this row:** `apps/web/lib/guests.ts` · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/_components/invited-to-chips.tsx` (NEW) · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/new/page.tsx` · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/[guestId]/page.tsx` · this CLAUDE.md row. **Test plan:** `pnpm -F web typecheck` clean for changed files (pre-existing `tests/e2e/*` Playwright errors unrelated) · `pnpm -F web lint` clean for changed files (2 pre-existing warnings unrelated) · auto-merge via `gh pr merge 433 --auto --merge` per [[feedback_setnayan_pr_auto_merge]] · merged on green within minutes of opening. **Sequencing note:** Fourth 2026-05-23 row · pure UX improvement on existing surfaces (no new routes · no new schema · no new SKU · no V1 launch impact · pilot-friendly since pilot cohort exercises the guest forms daily) · `.docx` mirror regen queued for next Cowork settling pass per established convention. |

Three locked architectural decisions: **(1) Multi-source asset library** — `moodboard_library_assets` adds `owner_kind TEXT CHECK (owner_kind IN ('setnayan','stylist','couple'))` + `owner_id UUID NULL`. RLS: `'setnayan'` rows readable by everyone, admin-only write (unchanged from today's behavior); `'stylist'` rows readable by the owning vendor + couples whose events have that stylist locked as vendor; `'couple'` rows readable by event hosts per iteration 0048 multi-host membership. Stylists get a private library (their portfolio shots · vendor sample books · color palettes they own) that no other stylist can see. **(2) Stylist sharing = PUSH model (owner-picked option C).** When a stylist is locked as a vendor on a couple's event, the stylist does NOT auto-share their full library; instead the stylist pins SPECIFIC assets to the couple's moodboard via a "Push to client" action in `/vendor-dashboard/stylist/library`. Protects stylist IP from "I'll hire someone else to copy this look" + keeps couple's experience focused on the curated set the stylist intentionally chose. **(3) Pinterest URL extraction = FREE for all couples (owner-picked option A).** Couples paste any pinterest.com/pin/* URL OR Instagram post URL OR vendor portfolio page URL → server-side Cloudflare Worker fetches the image + extracts 6-color palette + auto-suggests pillar (palette / location feel / dress codes) → inserts as `'couple'` row in `moodboard_library_assets`. Tone is advisory not prescriptive — couples can always proceed with any date; the Brain's job is to surface what's true about it, not override the couple's choice. **(4) Primary-layer resolution table.** Locks how the Brain picks which curated 2-3 reasons surface as the headline based on intake signals — Catholic ceremony + devout → Catholic / Liturgical primary · Chinese-Filipino household → Numerology primary (+ Catholic if applicable) · OFW-heavy guest list → Practical (homecoming alignment) · budget-conscious → Practical (Friday rates) · astrologically inclined → Western Astrology primary · default fallback → Practical (universally applicable). Mixed-faith / interfaith uses Practical primary + Catholic + Numerology layered as applicable. **(5) Strategic positioning.** No competitor in PH wedding-tech (The Knot · Zola · Joy · WedMeGood · Bridestory · Bride and Breakfast) ships layered cultural date-reasoning. WedMeGood gives generic Hindu calendar overlay only; the rest give a happy emoji. (2) `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/_components/wizard-cards/ceremony-venue-card.tsx` passed `events.venue_setting` (the host's RECEPTION venue type) into `fetchWizardVendorRecommendations` as a HARD filter. Result: any host with a non-heritage reception (banquet_hall / garden / beach / destination / outdoor_tent) saw the empty state. **Architectural error:** a ceremony venue's compatibility is about ceremony_type + faith, not the couple's reception style. Pivoted to `SET compatible_venue_settings = ARRAY[<7 reception settings>]` which achieves equivalent runtime behaviour without touching the schema. **Migration applied:** scoped via `WHERE user_id IS NULL AND services && ARRAY['religious_venue' OR 'officiant']` so any future real church account that claims its venue and intentionally sets compat tags is preserved. Idempotency keys on the `@>` superset check. **Belt-and-suspenders on Card 04 Officiant:** today every officiant in prod is tagged with all venue_settings (universal) so the code-side defensive pass changes nothing in current behaviour — but if a future seed narrows the tags the way the religious_venue seed did, Card 04 won't inherit the trap. **Post-fix verification:** Catholic + banquet_hall now returns **19** religious venues (was 0). Two patterns govern how vendor categories surface in the Concierge wizard vendor-pick grid + the marketplace browse: **Pattern A · Creations** (vendor sells multiple curated services that act as portfolio cards · couples pick "this look" / "this menu" / "this song set" · backed by `vendor_services` per [iteration 0045](0045_product_catalogs/0045_product_catalogs.md) · tile surfaces 3–5 portfolio photos cycling); **Pattern B · Locked** (vendor sells one fixed offering — a physical space, a person, a single rig, a single setup · tile shows one hero photo). Grid layout / search / filter / lock CTA / compare flow are IDENTICAL across both patterns — only tile content differs. **Category assignment (full table in [02_Specifications/Vendor_Taxonomy_V1_Master.md § 10](02_Specifications/Vendor_Taxonomy_V1_Master.md)):** **Creations** = Photographer · Videographer · SDE editor · Prenup shoot · Stylist · Florist · Catering · Cake · Attire (gown / suit / shoes / entourage / parents) · HMUA · Live band · Acoustic performer · Choir / quartet · DJ · Host/MC · Choreographer · Live painter · Calligrapher · Magician · Invitation designer · Stationery · Souvenirs · Rings · STD video editor. **Locked** = Reception venue · Ceremony venue · Officiant · Accommodation · Photobooth (per sub-tag) · Mobile bar (per sub-tag) · Pyrotechnics · Lights+Sound rig · Coordinator · Drone · Bridal car · Inflatable rentals. **Filter approach per pattern (locked same row):** **Region → City cascade** for Pattern B vendors with fixed addresses (Reception · parish-bound Officiant · stylist hub-city V1.x); **Distance from Reception** (10km initial · stepper) for Pattern B vendors anchored to Reception (Ceremony · Accommodation · Lights+Sound · Mobile Bar · Photobooth · Pyro · Drone); **Reviews-first · no geographic filter** for all Pattern A vendors + traveling Pattern B (Bridal Car · Coordinator). **V1 vs V1.1 split:** V1 ships with the spec lock + filter taxonomy correct + ONE photo per tile regardless of pattern (current behavior preserved). V1.1 follow-up PR upgrades Pattern A tiles to 3–5 photo carousel/collage sourced from `vendor_services.primary_photo_r2_key` — the grid primitive (`VendorPickGridCard`) is pattern-agnostic, the tile component branches based on a new `presentation_pattern` column added to `vendor_profiles` (or derived from category) in the V1.1 PR. **What ships this lock row:** corpus-only update — new § 10 added to `02_Specifications/Vendor_Taxonomy_V1_Master.md` (~70 lines · category assignment table + filter approach table + V1/V1.1 split + cross-references) + this CLAUDE.md row + existing § 10 maintenance log renumbered to § 11 with a new lock row appended. **What ships NEXT (queued PRs):** (a) Region → City cascade for Card 02 Reception · contained to `VendorPickGridCard` · ~1 day · (b) Attire expansion to 6 sub-categories (Bridal Gown · Groom's Suit · Bridal Shoes · Groom's Shoes · Entourage attire · Parents attire) · needs vendor_category enum migration + Card 18 multi-pick rewrite mirroring Card 14 Photobooths + Booths pattern · ~2 days · (c) Playlist builder for the booked DJ/band (free utility · syncs to vendor workspace · couple specifies first dance · parents dance · processional · cocktail playlist · banned songs) · placement: dedicated add-on surface at `/dashboard/[eventId]/add-ons/playlist` that gates open after Card 12 Music + Entertainment is locked · ~3 days · (d) V1.1 multi-photo tile upgrade against `VendorPickGridCard`. **Affected files this row:** `02_Specifications/Vendor_Taxonomy_V1_Master.md` (new § 10 + § 11 renumber + new maintenance log row) · CLAUDE.md (this row). **No engineering changes this row** — pure spec corpus update; These two statuses already exist in production schema · what's new is the behavioral semantics layered on top. **Rule 1 · Host-side cancel pre-downpayment.** Vendor detail page on host side at `/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors/[vendorId]` shows `[Cancel booking]` CTA when `event_vendors.status='contracted'` AND no `service_order_payments` row exists with `confirmed_at IS NOT NULL` for this vendor's bookings on this event. Click → confirmation modal → hard-delete `event_vendors` row + notification to vendor chat thread per [0019](0019_communications/0019_communications.md) + email per [0028](0028_email_notifications/0028_email_notifications.md) template `host_cancelled_booking` + date frees on vendor's calendar via `vendor_calendar_blocks` cleanup. Reversible (host can re-add via marketplace). Cancel CTA **HIDDEN** when `status='deposit_paid'` or later · replaced with `[Request refund/dispute]` CTA opening existing [0023 § 3.6 Disputes](0023_admin_console/0023_admin_console.md) flow. **Rule 2 · Vendor-side release pre-downpayment.** Vendor's `/vendor-dashboard/clients/[event_id]` page shows `[Release this booking]` CTA when no confirmed downpayment exists. Click → confirmation modal explaining host will be notified → `event_vendors` row hard-deletes + audit row inserts into NEW `vendor_release_history` table (release_id PK · event_vendor_id FK preserve-on-delete via separate column snapshot · vendor_profile_id · vendor_user_id · host_user_id · event_id snapshot · release_reason TEXT · vendor_notes TEXT NULL · released_at TIMESTAMPTZ) + chat thread notification + email per 0028 template `vendor_released_booking` to host + host's planning surface auto-refreshes with polite "{Vendor} couldn't take your booking after all — here are 3 similar vendors" suggestion strip pulling from existing 5-tier ranking ladder per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-24 seventh row. Vendor CANNOT release confirmed (downpaid) booking unilaterally · same as host side · dispute path only. Per owner-picked answer Q4: **free release, audit-logged only · no strike system · no release fee** · matches PH market reality where vendors politely back out routinely · `vendor_release_history` accumulates trend data for V1.x admin pattern analysis (10+ releases per vendor per month flags admin review for ghosting pattern). **Rule 3 · Pre-downpayment overlap default — vendor-configurable hold limit per date.** Per owner-picked answer Q2 ("Vendor sets a hold limit · e.g., max 3 per date"): new column `vendor_profiles.max_soft_holds_per_date INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK (max_soft_holds_per_date BETWEEN 1 AND 20)`. When host clicks Lock on a vendor via `finalizeVendor` server action, action checks count of existing `event_vendors` rows with same `vendor_profile_id` (joined via marketplace_vendor_id) + same event date (joined via events.wedding_date) + status='contracted' + archived_at IS NULL. If count >= `max_soft_holds_per_date`, action returns new status `'soft_hold_limit_reached'` with vendor's current limit + suggestion strip of 3 similar vendors. Vendor's `/vendor-dashboard/settings/availability` surface lets vendor adjust limit per-account-wide. Future V1.x: per-date override toggle on vendor's calendar (block this specific date from new inquiries · or raise/lower limit for this date only). Vendor sees badge `N soft holds` per date on `/vendor-dashboard/calendar` + expandable list of host names + event dates + "considering since" timestamps. **Rule 4 · Downpayment confirmation auto-releases other soft holds.** Per owner-picked answer Q3 ("Auto-release all others on downpayment"): when admin reconciles a downpayment via existing 0034 § 3.3 admin payment-confirm flow AND the downpayment links to an `event_vendor.event_vendor_id` (the existing payment-line-item → event-vendor mapping), system queries `event_vendors` for OTHER rows where same `vendor_profile_id` (joined via marketplace_vendor_id) + same event date (via events.wedding_date join) + status='contracted' + archived_at IS NULL + vendor_id != the confirming row's vendor_id. For each found row: hard-delete `event_vendors` + insert `vendor_release_history` audit row with release_reason='auto_released_on_downpayment' + send notification per 0028 template `auto_released_due_to_other_booking` to affected host + host's planning surface auto-refreshes with similar-vendors suggestion strip. Vendor gets summary notification: "Couple A's downpayment confirmed for {date} · released N other soft holds automatically · review vendor_release_history if needed." No fallback option (owner chose auto-release over manual decide-per-row · simpler UX · removes vendor's safety-net workflow but eliminates ghost holds completely · aligns with platform-discipline arc from CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 11 vendor reputation guardrails). **Rule 5 · Schedule-block primitive auto-created on hard lock.** Already speced per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row "Layout: Event-home planning cards" lock for `vendor_calendar_blocks` (30-min granularity per existing iteration 0022 spec). Once admin reconciles downpayment + Rule 4 fires, system also auto-creates a calendar block on vendor's `/vendor-dashboard/calendar` for the wedding window (start = wedding_date + venue_setup_hour · end = wedding_date + venue_teardown_hour · block_label = "Confirmed: {Couple Names}" · block_source='setnayan_booking' · is_private=FALSE so vendor's team can see it). Block links back to the `event_vendors` row · click → opens vendor's per-event workspace. **(3) Schema additions** (queued for migration · push BEFORE merge per [[feedback_setnayan_push_migrations_myself]]): `ALTER TABLE vendor_profiles ADD COLUMN max_soft_holds_per_date INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK (max_soft_holds_per_date BETWEEN 1 AND 20)` · `CREATE TABLE vendor_release_history` (10 columns per Rule 2 above · index on `(vendor_profile_id, released_at DESC)` for V1.x admin pattern queries · RLS: vendor reads their own rows · admin reads all rows · host reads their own event's rows for audit transparency). **(4) finalizeVendor server action extensions:** new return status `'soft_hold_limit_reached'` (per Rule 3) · existing 'hard_single_conflict' + 'already_locked' + 'not_found' + 'error' all preserved · UI handling in `plan-card-compare.tsx` performLock + `vendor-pick-grid-card.tsx` + `vendor-pick-card.tsx` for the new status (modal: "This vendor already has {N} confirmed soft holds for {date} · {Vendor} only takes {limit} simultaneous holds · here are 3 similar vendors who can take this date" + suggestion strip). **New server actions:** `cancelBookingAsHost(event_id, vendor_id)` (Rule 1 path · idempotent · returns 'already_deleted' if row missing OR 'downpaid_use_dispute_flow' if past soft-hold gate) · `releaseBookingAsVendor(event_id, vendor_id, reason, notes)` (Rule 2 path · vendor-authorized via existing vendor_team_members RLS · idempotent same shape). **Auto-trigger on payment confirmation:** new database trigger OR server-side cron-free sweep on `service_order_payments.confirmed_at` insert/update · checks for `event_vendor_id` linkage · fires Rule 4 cleanup if conditions met · idempotent on re-confirmation. **(5) UI surfaces:** Host side — `/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors/[vendorId]` gains conditional `[Cancel booking]` CTA per Rule 1 (status check + payment check). Two-layer separation: (a) `event_vendors.category` enum is unique per vendor-pick card (Card 02 Reception writes `'venue'` · Card 03 Ceremony writes `'religious_venue'` · etc. per `VENDOR_PICK_CATEGORY` map at `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/wizard-actions.ts:330-359`) so reception + ceremony picks never collide; (b) `events.wizard_state[task_id]` is JSONB keyed by task_id so each card writes to its own slot with task-specific metadata (event_vendor_id pointer · kind: 'marketplace'/'custom' · style/initials for monogram · slug/visibility for website · scheduled_date for prenup · etc.). Non-vendor cards write to dedicated `events.*` columns (event_date · role_palette.wizard_default · monogram_text + monogram_color · slug + landing_page_visibility). Multi-pick cards (14 Photobooths · 20 Sponsors) deliberately do NOT advance wizard_state on each lock — they wait for explicit [Mark done] CTA. **(2) Drift surfaced during the trace — 5 stale comment blocks in wizard-actions.ts claimed "Hard-single conflict check fires via the event_vendors trigger (PR #135 lineage)" but the trigger doesn't exist.** PR #135 was the multi-host event_moderators foundation (2026-05-19) and never touched event_vendors. No `BEFORE INSERT` trigger or unique constraint on `(event_id, category)` for hard-single categories. The only event_vendors uniqueness in any migration is `event_vendors_unique_directory_pick_per_event` which scopes to `source_venue_directory_id` not `category`. **In practice the wizard's serial resolver prevents lock-twice** because (a) once `wizard_state.<taskId>.completed_at` is stamped the WizardSequenceResolver hides the [Lock this vendor] button, and (b) `?card=<id>` URL state was retired 2026-05-23 per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 13. So the lock-twice risk only fires if someone bypasses the UI (direct server-action invocation OR stale-tab refresh race) and even then writes a silently-duplicated `event_vendors` row that the wizard's serial advancement would never have produced. **(3) Sentry 403 diagnosis.** Console shows `POST https://o4511393742782464.ingest.us.sentry.io/api/4511393744879616/envelope/ 403 (Forbidden)` originating from `apps/web/app/_components/deferred-observability.tsx:33` lazy-init reading `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`. The DSN value `cef1675c4317e863b04b9723fee423db` IS firing → env var IS set in Vercel prod. 403 from Sentry's envelope endpoint indicates one of three causes — most likely (a) public DSN key was rotated on Sentry side but Vercel still has the old key baked into the prod build · less likely (b) org/project billing quota exceeded · least likely (c) project disabled/moved. Diagnosis script (curl test independent of any deploy): `curl -i 'https://o4511393742782464.ingest.us.sentry.io/api/4511393744879616/envelope/?sentry_key=cef1675c4317e863b04b9723fee423db&sentry_version=7' -H 'content-type: application/x-sentry-envelope' --data-binary '{"event_id":"00000000000000000000000000000000","sent_at":"2026-05-28T00:00:00Z"}'`. 403 from the curl confirms the key itself is rejected at Sentry's edge → owner-side action at Sentry Dashboard → Settings → Projects → setnayan-web → Client Keys → copy current DSN → paste into Vercel `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` → redeploy. **Browser-extension noise** (the `message channel closed before a response was received` errors) is from a Chrome extension (Grammarly / 1Password / etc.), not Setnayan code. Extends v2.1 brief § 2.2 + § 3 monthly-only Pro lock (₱1,999/month). Vendor picks monthly OR annual at signup · annual gets a 17% discount + 1-payment-per-year cash-flow simplicity. SKU code `vendor_subscription_pro_annual` at 1999900 centavos · `time_recurrence='annual'` · `event_scope='all_events'` · `is_multi_purchase=FALSE` (one active subscription at a time) · stacks with token packs + Boosted Ads ₱1,200/wk + Sponsored Boost + Document Refresh ₱499 + On-site verification + content package per v2.1 § 5 vendor revenue model. **(4) Enterprise Vendor annual ₱54,999/yr · NEW v2.1 amendment SKU.** ~17% off vs monthly × 12 (₱5,499 × 12 = ₱65,988 · annual saves ₱10,989). Schema.org JSON-LD on `/for-vendors` adds 2 new `Offer` blocks (4 total: Pro monthly + Pro annual + Enterprise monthly + Enterprise annual · prevents the eighth-row schema.org JSON-LD undersell trap). All BIR-receipt copy unchanged · 0% commission copy unchanged · 100-token-on-verification copy unchanged. **(7) Why annual subscriptions matter strategically.** Annual is the standard SaaS retention lever — 12-month commitment reduces churn + increases ARR predictability for the platform + simplifies vendor cash-flow planning (1 payment vs 12). The 17% discount anchor matches typical SaaS annual-vs-monthly conventions (Notion 16% · Linear 20% · Webflow 20% · Stripe Atlas 20% · Shopify 25%) · sits mid-range · doesn't anchor cheap (>20%) doesn't anchor stingy (<10%). The ₱19,999 + ₱54,999 charm-priced endings match the locked Pricing.md § 1 charm convention from CLAUDE.md 2026-05-12 row (-1 endings on round prices). **(8) Verification-fee retirement rationale.** Per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16 row 8 the verification fees were modeled as ongoing-cost defense (admin labor + KYC API + sanctions screening = ~₱535/vendor + ~₱200/yr recurring per Persona/Veriff/Onfido renewal). v2.1's one-time lifetime badge reframes verification as a CAC investment (Setnayan absorbs the ~₱535 once · earns it back via Pro/Enterprise subscription LTV · no recurring vendor fee needed). Demotion-recovery fee retirement reflects that disputes already route through 0023 § 6 with admin moderation · adding a re-verification fee is redundant friction on already-disciplined vendors (the demotion itself is the consequence · no need to double-tax with a fee). Net financial impact: Setnayan forgoes ₱1,499/yr × verified vendor count (e.g., 1,000 verified vendors = ₱1.5M/yr foregone) BUT gains LTV via Pro/Enterprise subscription stickiness from the annual discount mechanic · trade is roughly margin-neutral at scale + simplifies the vendor onboarding pitch (one fee, one badge, forever). **(9) Affected files** (spec corpus this row · engineering deferred to Phase L8). | 2026-05-28 | **Twelfth 2026-05-28 row · perf optimization shipped via PR [#567](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/567) · event-home `/dashboard/[eventId]` 4 sequential round trips → 2 · ~150-600ms TTFB win on every render.** Owner asked why auto-login to dashboard loads materially slower than Facebook home page. Diagnosed against the 1976-line event-home server component as 4 sequential Supabase round trips before first paint: Round 1 (top Promise.all · 18 queries · parallel) → Round 2 (`compatibilityFetches` · 4 queries · parallel) → Round 3 (SERIAL `vendor_services` cross-category fetch) → Round 6 (SERIAL `[fetchEventActivity, fetchAttributedActivity]` Promise.all) → Round 7 (SERIAL `fetchUpcomingItems`). **Fix:** lifted the three serial awaits into the existing parallel rounds — `fetchEventActivity` + `fetchAttributedActivity` into round 1 (only need `eventId` + `user.id` available at start) · cross-category `vendor_services` fetch into round 2 (depends only on `marketplaceIds` from round 1, ready BEFORE compat lookups) · `fetchUpcomingItems` into round 2 (depends only on `event.event_date` + `event.ceremony_type` from round 1's `eventRes`). Net: 4 sequential rounds → 2. At Supabase Singapore RTT ~50-200ms from PH, saves ~150-600ms on every event-home render. **Safety:** same `.catch()` / IIFE try/catch with `logQueryError` + safe-default shapes as the existing fetchers (6th hotfix pass · Path B 2026-05-23) · a throw in any single fetcher degrades just that lane to empty data (same as today) · same admin-client gating for cross-category services + attributed activity (the parent `event_vendors` / `event_action_log` queries already enforce the host's RLS · admin reads are safe). **No schema change** · no new dependencies · no UX change · `+142/-91` net diff on `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/page.tsx` · `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm lint` clean. **Comparison framing for the owner question:** Facebook home loads faster because of global CDN + warm edge servers + decade of streaming-hydration tuning — Setnayan can't match that, but the 3 of 4 round trips that were stacked sequentially for no architectural reason within Setnayan's own stack are now collapsed. Auto-merged on green per [[feedback_setnayan_pr_auto_merge]] · pilot 2026-06-01 scope UNCHANGED (this lands as polish 4 days before launch · acceptable to revert if any regression surfaces). **Entry points** (per [[feedback_setnayan_orphan_prevention]]): `/dashboard/[eventId]` reachable from `/dashboard` root redirect (primary event auto-jump) + event-switcher chrome + direct URL bookmarks · no new routes · no new components · no new server actions · all downstream readers of `crossCategoryServicesRaw`, `upcoming`, `activity`, `attributedActivity` use same variable names + types. **Cross-references:** CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 11 (Unified QR Code Lifecycle Model · event-home as primary host surface) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-23 6th hotfix pass · Path B (graceful-degrade contract preserved) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row "Home is the guide" (the 65-card wizard + Your Plan grid + activity feed + UpcomingSchedules + MoneyInFlight all render on this surface · heavy query load supports the rich UX) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-23 row 1 (Google + Facebook OAuth providers · the auto-login flow this perf pass speeds up) · [[project_setnayan_pilot_timeline]] · [[feedback_setnayan_document_changes_with_why]]. **`.docx` mirror regenerated alongside this row** per established convention (pandoc at `~/.local/bin/pandoc` v3.9.0.2 per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row 450). **Sequencing note:** Twelfth 2026-05-28 row · pilot polish · engineering shipped + spec catch-up landed in same session · no schema migration · no SKU/pricing change · no V1 launch scope expansion · 11 prior 2026-05-28 rows preserved (tenth row v2.1 brief stays canonical · eleventh row annual SKUs stays canonical · this row extends both with the perf-pass surface optimization). |

| 2026-05-29 | **2 pilot blockers diagnosed + fixed in one session via PR [#614](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/614) (MERGED) — admin console crash + shop console redirect-loop.** Owner-reported 3 days before pilot 2026-06-01: *"Cannot see the vendor dashboard via shop console. Admin console said something went wrong, and it does not load also."* Reproduced both locally via dev-server stub-bypass; net +40/-2 across 2 files. **Bug 1 · /admin throws on every authed render.** `apps/web/app/admin/_components/admin-bottom-nav.tsx` shipped as a Server Component (no `'use client'` directive) that built `ADMIN_BOTTOM_NAV_ITEMS` as a const array of `{key, label, href, icon: LucideIcon, activeMatch}` entries, then passed the array as a prop to `<BottomNav>` — the Client Component primitive from PR #603 nav phase 0. Lucide icons are `forwardRef` objects (`$$typeof` + `render`); Next.js can't serialize them across the Server→Client prop boundary so the admin layout threw into the root error boundary (`apps/web/app/error.tsx` "Something on our end didn't work · We've logged the issue ..."). Dev-server stub-bypass repro confirmed the exact error verbatim: `Error: Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components unless you explicitly expose it by marking it with "use server"... {$$typeof: ..., render: function House}` (also LayoutList, Users, DollarSign, Menu). Fix: mark `admin-bottom-nav.tsx` as `'use client'` so the icon refs stay on the client side and never traverse the boundary. Symmetric with `admin-sidebar.tsx` which has been `'use client'` since PR #606 for exactly the same reason. Inline WHY block added so future agents extending the admin nav don't drop the directive. Verified: stubbed /admin response flipped 500 → 200 with full chrome rendering ("Setnayan · Admin" / "Switch view" / Queues / Money / Operations all present). Root cause: PR #606 (Phase 3 admin IA · merged 2026-05-29T06:02Z) introduced the new client-primitive `BottomNav` + new wrapper `admin-bottom-nav.tsx` simultaneously; typecheck + lint + build all pass with the wrapper as a Server Component because the type system has no way to detect the RSC serialization constraint statically; the regression only surfaces on actual authed render (none of CI's headless fetches reach the post-auth path). **Bug 2 · /vendor-dashboard redirect-loops §10a Internal Accounts.** `apps/web/app/vendor-dashboard/layout.tsx` line 53-56 gated entry on the rigid `profile?.account_type !== 'vendor'` predicate. But the always-visible role pill (`apps/web/app/_components/role-switch-pill.tsx:82-95`) offers the Shop console target whenever `roles.hasVendorAccess` is TRUE — computed in `apps/web/lib/roles.ts:165-167` as "owns a vendor_profile OR sits on any vendor_team_members row" independent of account_type. Net: §10a Internal Account (`is_internal=TRUE` per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-12 row "Owner / Internal Accounts — permanent unlimited-use grants locked", account_type typically 'admin') who also owns a vendor_profile for pilot dogfooding saw Shop console in the pill, clicked it, got silently bounced back to /dashboard. Same path lit up for any dual-role user (vendor team-member on someone else's profile + customer on their own events). Fix: swap the predicate to `!roles.hasVendorAccess`. The roles summary is already fetched in the same `Promise.all` so this is a zero-cost predicate change. Aligns the layout's gate with the canonical access rule the role pill enforces. Per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-15 dual-role lock ("a single users row may carry account_type='vendor' AND own/host events as a customer · Vendor application is additive") + 2026-05-20 Login-landing rule lock ("admin + vendor consoles reached via role-switch pill only") — the role pill IS the canonical access gate, and any console layout must accept users the pill grants access to. **Engineering process notes.** Both bugs were initially invisible because (a) typecheck + lint + production build all pass clean (no static detection of RSC serialization constraints OR semantic-only access-gate drift); (b) the only CI runtime check (Playwright e2e) doesn't have an authed admin journey wired up; (c) the unauthed fetch path renders 307 redirect via the early `if (!user) redirect(...)` so curl-based smoke tests never reach the crash. Root cause identification took ~25 min of dev-server stub-bypass — patched the admin layout to inject a fake authed profile, then fetched /admin to see the actual runtime error, which immediately surfaced the lucide forwardRef serialization message. Logged as a process improvement for future RSC nav primitive landings: any time a Server Component holds an array literal containing component refs and passes it to a Client Component prop, add the `'use client'` directive to the wrapper file by default (or refactor to pass primitive keys instead of refs). **Scope.** No schema migration · no SKU/pricing change · no V1 scope expansion · pilot 2026-06-01 unblocked. PR #614 auto-merged on green (per `[[feedback_setnayan_pr_auto_merge]]`). Branch + worktree cleaned up post-merge. **Cross-references.** [PR #606](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/606) `feat(nav phase 3): admin console IA` (the regression-introducing PR) · [PR #603](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/603) `feat(nav): Phase 0 shared nav primitives` (defines the BottomNav client primitive) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-15 dual-role lock + 2026-05-20 Login-landing rule lock (the role-pill access model that the vendor-dashboard guard must align with) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-12 §10a Internal Accounts lock (the owner-account configuration that triggered Bug 2). Per `[[feedback_setnayan_document_changes_with_why]]` this row carries the canonical WHY for both fixes; per `[[feedback_setnayan_orphan_prevention]]` no new orphans (`/admin` still reachable from role-pill Admin console target · `/vendor-dashboard` still reachable from role-pill Shop console target with broader-access predicate). **`.docx` mirror regenerated alongside this row** via pandoc per established convention (pandoc available at `~/.local/bin/pandoc` v3.9.0.2 per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row 450). **Sequencing note:** Pure pilot-polish row · 1 PR shipped + merged · no schema · no SKU/pricing · no scope expansion · pilot 2026-06-01 unblocked.

(5) Checked `git log origin/main` · spotted PR #624 "fix(build): unblock Vercel deploys · ESLint rule reference removed" which fixed a DIFFERENT build error from my own Buckets 5 + 7 (I had used `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` referencing a rule the project's ESLint config — `next/core-web-vitals` only — doesn't register · this caused `next build` to fail with "Definition for rule '@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any' was not found"). (6) Pushed an empty commit `29127ce` to force a fresh Vercel build. (7) CI ran on the empty commit · `production build` STILL failed · pulled the GitHub Actions log · found a SECOND build error from PR #623 (V2 Phase G offline daemon): `./app/admin/offline/page.tsx · Error: ssr: false is not allowed with next/dynamic in Server Components. Please move it into a Client Component.` PR #623 had landed `const OfflineDiagnostic = dynamic(() => import('./_components/offline-diagnostic'), { ssr: false, ... })` directly inside the page export, which is forbidden in Next.js 15 because the page exports `metadata` (making it a Server Component). PR #624 hadn't caught this · only fixed my ESLint references. **(8) Built the Next.js 15 canonical wrapper-pattern fix** in `claude/fix-offline-page-ssr-false`: new `apps/web/app/admin/offline/_components/offline-diagnostic-loader.tsx` Client Component (`'use client';`) that hosts the `dynamic({ ssr: false })` call · page.tsx imports the wrapper instead of calling `dynamic()` directly · server page keeps `export const metadata` working. (9) Local `pnpm -F web build` passed cleanly (exit 0 · /venue/[slug] compiled to 2.73 kB · 115 kB First Load JS). (10) Parallel agent shipped the SAME fix at the same time via **PR #626** ("fix(build): wrap admin/offline dynamic import in client component") using a slightly different naming (`OfflineDiagnosticLoader` function export vs my `OfflineDiagnostic` const re-export · both equally valid). PR #626 merged first · my branch became identical to main · `gh pr create` failed with "No commits between main and claude/fix-offline-page-ssr-false" which is the correct outcome. (11) Pushed another empty commit `d49a274` to trigger a fresh Vercel build now that both ESLint AND Server Component blockers are resolved. (12) Polling for deploy completion · expecting `venue=3 · vendors=2 · pricing=2` ld+json blocks per page when the build lands. **The real lesson:** when 4+ PRs merge within 10 minutes (08:11 → 08:20Z on 2026-05-29) AND a build-breaking change is in main BEFORE the SEO PRs, **all subsequent PRs deploy "successfully" from a code-on-main perspective but never reach production** because Vercel serves the last successful build for all routes that compiled in it. Vercel's GitHub status check appears under `production build` (GitHub Actions) — when that fails, the matching Vercel deploy also fails, but the deploy failure is silent unless someone checks the Vercel dashboard. **PR #624 fixed ONE of TWO build-blockers · I introduced one of them (Buckets 5+7 ESLint reference) · PR #623 introduced the other (offline page Server Component) · neither author caught the other's issue.** PR #626 fixed the second one ~3hr after the sprint closed · my empty commit re-triggered the build. **Pattern lock for future SEO/JSON-LD work in this repo:** (a) NEVER use `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` · this project's ESLint config doesn't register the `@typescript-eslint` plugin · use `Record<string, unknown>` typing instead OR no comment at all and let TS infer. (b) NEVER use `dynamic({ ssr: false })` inside a Server Component (anything that exports `metadata` or doesn't have `'use client'`) · always wrap in a Client Component module. (c) After a big merge burst, **always curl the live HTML** to verify the changes are actually rendering before declaring the sprint complete. The owner's GSC inspection caught this · I declared the sprint complete prematurely · production state did not match `origin/main`. (d) **Add a smoke test to CI**: a post-build check that curls each public route and verifies the expected JSON-LD block count. Would have caught this at deploy time. | 2026-05-29 | **🎯 VENDOR DISCOVERY ARCHITECTURE LOCK · 5 coupled refinements span Card 04 Officiant auto-resolve + bundle expansion to shortlist + vendor service price ranges + shortlist budget total + per-user persistent favorites · all V1.x post-pilot scope · pilot 2026-06-01 in 3 days UNCHANGED.** Closes the multi-turn Filipino taxonomy + vendor discovery conversation 2026-05-29 evening. Owner directives across the conversation: (a) *"officiants should be provided by the church and precana? so can we just remove them?"* → DON'T remove · auto-resolve instead · (b) *"auto resolve. also when vendors provide bundles that include multiple services, they can add them to the short list. so we can also place the total budget. If there is a range. then budget should also show in range based on their chosen shortlist."* · (c) *"yes we do have shortlist as discussed before. also favorites so they will show everytime they create a new event in the future"* · (d) *"yes do them now."* Consolidates 5 locks into one architectural row per the established "Vendor Discovery Architecture" framing. **(1) Card 04 Officiant auto-resolve.** Catholic + parish church match (`event_vendors` religious_venue locked + `venue_directory.compatible_ceremony_types[]` contains `'catholic'`) → "Officiant provided by {Parish Name}, confirmed via Pre-Cana" status surface (no vendor pick required · Mark-Done CTA). Civil + locked venue with `venue_setting='civil_registrar'` → "Provided by {City Hall/Municipal Hall}" status. INC + INC chapel match → "Provided by {INC Chapel}" status. All other combinations (Christian non-bundle / Muslim / Cultural / Mixed / destination / Catholic-at-non-church) → standard vendor picker. "Bring your own officiant" override affordance ALWAYS available for the real PH edge cases (interfaith ceremonies · family priest from a different parish with permission letter · retired pastor · destination celebrant · NCR civil-with-hired-celebrant trend). Reads `events.ceremony_type` + the locked `event_vendors` row for `religious_venue` canonical_service to detect bundle case. Mirrors the religion-adaptive copy pattern from CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 9 PR #314 — different state per event signals, taxonomy stays intact. Card 04 stays as canonical Wizard task in the 48-card sequence; the surface just renders Mark-Done CTA instead of picker when auto-resolve fires. The 192-canonical taxonomy stays locked — auto-resolve is a UX layer that maps event context to "bundled" vs "vendor-pick" states without changing the underlying taxonomy structure. **(2) Bundle expansion to multi-row shortlist** (extends CLAUDE.md 2026-05-24 seventh row package-inclusion from `status='locked'` to also cover `status='considering'`). When a host shortlists a vendor whose `vendor_services.included_services TEXT[]` lists OTHER canonical_services, those services auto-populate as `event_vendors` rows with `inclusion_source='package'` + `parent_vendor_id=<vendor>` + `parent_package_id=<vendor_service>` + `status='considering'`. Plan grid cells render "✓ Considering with {Vendor Name}'s {Package Name}" cream-tinted chip styling (visually distinct from emerald-tinted locked-package chip from 2026-05-24 row). Removing the parent shortlist row auto-removes all bundle-included shortlist rows via cascading delete. Schema: status enum + `event_vendors.inclusion_source` + `parent_vendor_id` + `parent_package_id` columns from 2026-05-24 seventh row already cover this — only the auto-population trigger needs extension to fire on `status='considering'` INSERTs (currently the trigger fires only on `status='locked'`). **(3) Vendor service price ranges.** Schema: `ALTER TABLE vendor_services ADD COLUMN price_max_centavos INT NULL CHECK (price_max_centavos IS NULL OR price_max_centavos >= base_price_centavos)` (existing `base_price_centavos` becomes canonical min · NULL `price_max` = single price · non-NULL = range). Vendor-side UI on `/vendor-dashboard/services/[id]` gains a "Quote a range" toggle that exposes min + max inputs when active (single price the default · range opt-in). Display: `price_max IS NULL` → single "₱X" / `price_max IS NOT NULL` → range "₱X–₱Y". Existing fixed-price services stay valid (no backfill needed). RLS unchanged. **(4) Shortlist budget total + range math (new surface).** New `<ShortlistBudgetCard>` component on event-home + per-cell sub-totals on Plan grid. Math: `min_total = SUM(price_min)` and `max_total = SUM(COALESCE(price_max, price_min))` across `event_vendors` rows where `status IN ('considering','contracted','deposit_paid')` for the active event. Display rules: all rows have NULL `price_max` → single "Shortlist total: ₱X" / any row has `price_max IS NOT NULL` → range "Shortlist total: ₱X–₱Y" / mixed locked vs considering → segment breakdown ("₱180,000 locked + ₱120,000–₱250,000 considering · ₱300,000–₱430,000 total"). Compares against `events.wedding_budget_centavos` if set ("₱350,000–₱500,000 of ₱600,000 budget" + progress bar with min anchor + max range whisker). Stays SEPARATE from iteration [0007 Budget & Expenses](0007_budget_expenses/0007_budget_expenses.md) canonical ledger which tracks locked + paid line items only — no conflation between the locked-budget ledger (0007) and the running-shortlist-estimate surface (this row). New helper `lib/shortlist-budget.ts` computes min/max totals + delta against budget cap. **(5) Favorites — persistent per-user across events (new feature surface).** New table `user_favorite_vendors` (user_id UUID FK · vendor_profile_id UUID FK · canonical_service TEXT snapshot for filter · favorited_from_event_id UUID FK NULL for audit trail · notes TEXT NULL for host's personal note · favorited_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()) with composite PK `(user_id, vendor_profile_id)`. Indexes: `(user_id, favorited_at DESC)` for chronological listing + `(vendor_profile_id)` for vendor-side "Favorited by N couples" stat. RLS: user reads/writes own rows only. **Multi-host events (iteration 0048) keep each host's favorites private — favorites are personal taste, not event-shared** (different from shortlist which IS event-shared across multi-host per existing 0048 visibility tags). New surfaces: (a) Heart/Save button (Lucide Heart icon) on marketplace vendor cards + `/v/[slug]` profile + shortlist rows in Plan grid · (b) New `/dashboard/favorites` listing grouped by canonical_service with quick "Add to current event" action per row (when host is inside an event context) · (c) **NEW Tier 0 "From your favorites"** inserted above existing Tier 1 venue-recommended in the CLAUDE.md 2026-05-24 seventh-row 5-tier recommendation ladder (now 6-tier) — surfaces on wizard cards + Plan grid + marketplace search · (d) Compatibility chip overlay (PR #315 pattern) when a favorite's `vendor_profiles.compatible_ceremony_types[]` / `compatible_venue_settings[]` mismatches current event context (e.g., *"This favorite serves Catholic ceremonies — your wedding is civil. Tap to override."*) · (e) New-event creation flow surfaces "Your favorites" strip across every category that has at least one saved vendor — matches Filipino-household reality of vendor relationships compounding across events (caterer they used for Tita's 60th anniversary · photographer who shot the parents' silver anniversary · florist from cousin's debut). **Strategic moat note.** Favorites is real structural defensibility — WedMeGood + The Knot + Zola + Bridestory + Joy don't carry vendor relationships across events. Filipino household reality (parents' anniversaries / wedding / baptism / debut / 60th / wedding-of-cousin all flow through the same family vendor circle) makes per-user persistent favorites disproportionately sticky in PH market. Vendors get a structural reason to deliver well beyond a single event — they get permanent placement in family planning vocabulary. **Schema additions (one consolidated migration).** `ALTER TABLE vendor_services ADD COLUMN price_max_centavos INT NULL CHECK (...)` · `CREATE TABLE user_favorite_vendors (...)` with RLS policies per `02_Specifications/RLS_Policy_Pattern.md` patterns · auto-population trigger extension for `status='considering'` bundle-on-shortlist per § (2). City = `vendor_profiles.location_city`. Canonical Service Display Label = `canonical_service_schemas.display_name_en` lookup on `vendor_profiles.services[0]` (primary canonical service). ID = monotonic increment within `(city, canonical_service)` namespace via new sequence table `vendor_screen_name_sequences`. Slug derived as `kebab-case(screen_name)` → e.g. `manila-wedding-photographer-4218` → used as the public microsite URL at `/v/[slug]` so the URL itself doesn't leak the real `business_slug`. **(3) Persistence rule.** Once screen_name generates on vendor signup, it persists forever — no regeneration if vendor changes services array, location city, or business name. Otherwise returns `vendor.screen_name`.
